newsitem.title: USA: Venture sees $3.50/shr charge in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Venture sees $3.50/shr charge in Q2.

text.p: Venture Stores Inc said it will take a one-time noncash charge against earnings in the second quarter of $3.50 per share on costs tied to the sale of 20 stores to Kmart Corp, and on inventory liquidation.
The retailer said it has hired the investment banking firm of Houlihan, Lokey, Howard & Zukin "to identify additional potential sources of capital for Venture."
The company said it is working with Kimco Realty Corp "to capitalize on real estate opportunities."

Kimco chief executive Milton Cooper said, "Venture has significant value in its real estate portfolio and we will be providing counsel on how to leverage those assets for additional funding and improved shareholder value."

In addition, Venture said it is discussing an amendment to its credit facility to accommodate the second-quarter charge against earnings. The discussions are occuring with BT Commercial Corp, the agent for the facility, Venture said.
"BT had advised Venture that, in light of the noncash nature of the charge, an appropriate amendment should be obtained in the ordinary course," Venture said.
Venture said it will operate 93 stores in nine states after the sale of the 20 stores to Kmart is completed.
Terms of the store sale were not disclosed.
